To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) spreading activation is a short-term process that does not persist over long periods; (b) spreading activation does not persist long enough to produce the false alarms in the DRM paradigm; (c) the false recognition obtained on the DRM task is due to the reactivation of a study list’s associative structure when a related probe item is presented and the subject is in a retrieval mode; (d) the retrieval mode is created when the subject has episodic retrieval instructions, and (e)
the time course of spreading activation in the DRM paradigm does not match the time course of false recognition in that paradigm.
